articles.title: Your vulnerability scanner is a dependency too: pin it
articles.excerpt: On March 19, an attacker published Trivy v0.69.4 with stolen credentials. The same evening, they moved 76 of the 77 tags of the trivy-action action to a secret stealer. The scanner meant to protect pi…
articles.body: On March 19, an attacker published Trivy v0.69.4 with stolen credentials. The same evening, they moved 76 of the 77 tags of the trivy-action action to a secret stealer. The scanner meant to protect pipelines stole their secrets for twelve hours. After that, I counted the action references in my own repositories: 689, and zero pinned to a SHA. TL;DR : your security scanner runs inside your CI, with the job's secrets. It is a dependency, and the Trivy attack proved it. Pin every action to a full commit SHA, every image to its digest, and ban latest . Keep Dependabot or Renovate to bump the pins. My audit: 689 action references, 0 by SHA, 170 on @main . Figures, SHAs and digests as of November 3, 2026. Check them before copying.
articles.author: Jules Robineau

articles.title: Building a Document Pipeline for International Credential Recognition (Apostille + Certified Translation)
articles.excerpt: If you've ever built an onboarding flow, a visa-processing tool, or an HR platform for international hires, you've probably run into the mess that is cross-border document verification. Credential rec…
articles.body: If you've ever built an onboarding flow, a visa-processing tool, or an HR platform for international hires, you've probably run into the mess that is cross-border document verification. Credential recognition — getting a foreign degree accepted by a government authority — is one of the gnarlier versions of this problem, and Germany's professional recognition system is a good case study for why. The source article on certified diploma translation for Germany covers the legal and procedural side well: sworn vs. certified translation, apostille requirements, which authority wants what. This post is about the other half of the problem — how you'd actually model and automate this as a workflow if you're building tooling around it.

articles.title: Secure Your APIs: OAuth2 and JWT for Beginners
articles.excerpt: Securing an API usually turns into one of the fiddliest parts of backend work, and this JetBrains tutorial by Mdu Sibisi breaks it down for Kotlin and Spring Boot developers. It starts with the basics…
articles.body: Securing an API usually turns into one of the fiddliest parts of backend work, and this JetBrains tutorial by Mdu Sibisi breaks it down for Kotlin and Spring Boot developers. It starts with the basics of how OAuth2 and JWTs fit together: OAuth2 handles delegated access, JWTs are the signed tokens that carry the identity and permissions, and your API only needs to check the "badge," not issue it. From there it builds a small document API, adds a custom converter to pull roles and permissions out of the token, and uses @PreAuthorize so access rules stay out of controller code. It also covers checking the issuer and audience claims, so tokens meant for a different app or environment get rejected.

articles.title: Lullwood: How Many Trees Can three.js Render? 5,200, With Chunked InstancedMesh
articles.excerpt: Lullwood, our free browser horror game, draws a 5,200-tree forest by splitting it into 64 chunks, giving each chunk its own trio of three.js InstancedMesh objects, and building only the chunks near th…
articles.body: Lullwood, our free browser horror game, draws a 5,200-tree forest by splitting it into 64 chunks, giving each chunk its own trio of three.js InstancedMesh objects, and building only the chunks near the player: 25 at spawn, 36 at most while walking. The heaviest whole frame we measured was 101,996 triangles. Drawn as one pool, the trees alone would be 270,400. Here is how it works and what we could not measure. One pool, never culled The forest is 5,200 trees on a 480-unit map. A tree is three meshes: a six-sided CylinderGeometry trunk and two seven-sided ConeGeometry foliage cones. The first version drew every tree from one InstancedMesh pool covering the whole map.

articles.title: An SSH agent can hold a key without granting every destination
articles.excerpt: An SSH agent can hold a key without granting every destination An SSH agent is convenient because a private key can stay in one process while many terminals request signatures. The usual risk is broad…
articles.body: An SSH agent can hold a key without granting every destination An SSH agent is convenient because a private key can stay in one process while many terminals request signatures. The usual risk is broad: if every client can ask the agent for the same key, a compromised jump host or session inherits access to every server that accepts it. OpenSSH added destination-constrained keys to narrow that delegation, but the constraint only helps when the key is loaded and managed correctly. ssh-add(1) documents the -h destination_constraint option. The OpenSSH project's agent-restriction design says destination constraints were added in OpenSSH 8.9 and that keys are not constrained by default.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
articles.excerpt: See the most epic photos from SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and historic launch tower catch.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

articles.body: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday , Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters . The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." articles.title: NASA Receives 16th Consecutive ‘Clean’ Financial Audit Opinion
articles.excerpt: For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion…
articles.body: Credit: NASA For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion, certifying that NASA’s financial statements conform with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for federal agencies and accurately present the agency’s financial position. “Our responsibility at NASA is to be disciplined stewards of the resources entrusted to us by the American people while delivering on the missions they expect from this agency,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.
